author: haiku
label: baseline-dev-01
changes: Added a short "Terms used" section defining token, SHA-256 hash, transaction, row lock, queue and worker, password hash, and breached-password list, so a reader new to the stack can follow the design.

Rewrote the request-flow diagram's step labels in plain words (for example "find user by email", "lock the user row", "invalidate older links") and moved the rate-limit stop branch into the diagram as a clear reply line.

Rewrote the link-click diagram so the GET branch shows the two outcomes (form or expired page) explicitly, and labeled each POST step (token re-check, password check, hashing, transaction, lock, updates, logout, commit, email) in order.
Expanded the request-flow notes to explain why the response is padded, why the row lock makes the cap exact, why step 5 runs only after the limit check, and what happens if adding the job fails.

Expanded the link-click notes to explain why GET writes nothing (email scanners), why the POST checks the token twice, what the single transaction guarantees, and why the token is kept out of the URL after the GET.

Changed the data section to state retention, token generation (32 random bytes, 43 URL-safe characters), and queue exposure in plain terms, with the config values in one place, and clarified the invalidated_at comment.
Rewrote the failure paths as short, self-contained sentences, stating the user-visible result and the data effect for each, without changing any behavior.
Reworded the open decisions for clarity, including explaining that the outbox pattern means writing the job in the same transaction as the link, and kept all four open questions and their defaults.
Added a "What this does" intro and a "The parts" section that name each existing component in plain words before the flows use them.
Expanded the terms list: added "link states" (usable = unused, not invalidated, not expired) and "transaction", and gave each term a plain definition.
Replaced the repeated lists of link conditions with the single term "usable", defined once and used throughout.
Trimmed the request-flow diagram: one reply arrow per branch instead of several, and branch explanations moved into the notes so the arrows stay readable.

Turned the inline comments in the request and click diagrams into numbered notes that explain the reasons behind each step (why the GET writes nothing, why the token is checked twice, why steps 6 to 8 share one transaction).
Stated in the outbox open decision that the queue does not currently live in Postgres, which is the fact the decision depends on.
Kept all requirements, numbers, table definitions, failure paths and open decisions unchanged in substance.
Added a plain-language sentence to each term and parts entry (queue, worker, invalidated, used, rolling hour, outbox pattern) so a reader outside the project can follow them.
Split the request-flow diagram into the main path only. Failure branches were removed from the diagram and are now stated as numbered steps and in section 4, so the arrows stay readable and aligned.
Listed the steps inside the request-flow transaction (2 to 7) as numbered text, including the cap check and the early COMMIT with no changes when the limit is reached.
Reworded the link-click diagram to the GET and POST exchange only, and moved the POST steps into a numbered list, since the old inline steps were hard to follow in a diagram.
Clarified that the hourly count includes links that were later invalidated or whose email later failed, which the old note implied but did not state.
Replaced 'burn' with 'used' and defined 'invalidated' separately, so the two states are not confused.
Tightened the failure paths to one line each, stating the user-visible result and the data change.
Fixed misaligned and overlong ASCII arrows and labels in all three diagrams.
Spelled out the 'passwords' config value as 12 characters and the retry behaviour as waits that grow each time, instead of 'backoff'.
